aspects.says: jPOS is AGPL v3: a modified version that users interact with over a network must offer them its source, even if it is never distributed, unless a commercial licence is bought.
basis: section:1.4. jPOS Is AGPL: Network Users of Your Modified Version Are Offered Its Source

aspects.says: The course runs jPOS 2.1.7 while jpos.org describes jPOS 3, so examples from jpos.org may not compile against it.
basis: section:1.5. This Course Runs jPOS 2.1.7, and jpos.org Describes jPOS 3
aspects.reason: a fact about the course's set-up that the reader meets when building, not an idea to be checked

aspects.says: The standard fixes what a field means, while each network's dialect fixes its encoding and the transport frames it, so two systems that both follow ISO 8583 cannot necessarily read each other.
basis: section:1.2. The Standard Fixes What a Field Means, and Each Link Fixes Its Bytes

aspects.says: The first MTI digit names the edition, and fields change between editions: a 1993 approval is 000 in field 39, which a 1987 check reads as a decline.
basis: section:1.3. The First MTI Digit Names the Edition, and Editions Disagree on Fields

aspects.says: A message is an MTI, a bitmap and only the fields the bitmap marks, in field-number order, so a field's position depends on every field before it.
basis: section:1.1. A Message Is an MTI, a Bitmap and the Fields the Bitmap Announces

aspects.says: A program prints or logs a card number only through ISOUtil.protect, never in clear.
aspects.reason: a habit the page introduces with its first program; masking in jPOS's logs is unit 8's subject, and a test here would only check that the reader retyped one call
